lesson_title: Five HIV Myths in Sixty Seconds
hook_text: Can you get HIV from a hug, a shared cup or a mosquito? Five quick myths, five straight answers.
clip_script: Myth one: you can get HIV from hugging. False. It is not spread by touch. Myth two: sharing a cup or a toilet seat spreads it. False. Myth three: mosquitoes carry it. False. HIV spreads through sex without a condom, through shared needles, and from mother to baby without treatment. Myth four: HIV and AIDS are the same. False. HIV is the virus that attacks your body's germ-fighting cells. AIDS is the late stage that can come years later without treatment. Myth five: you can tell by looking. False. Many people have no symptoms, so the only way to know is a free, private test at a clinic. The good news: daily treatment called ART keeps people healthy for a long life. And the safest choice of all for young people is to wait.
visual_style: Whiteboard myth cards flipping to big FALSE stamps; a simple shield of white blood cells; a clinic sign with a confidential test icon.
pacing: Rapid myth-busting rhythm, then a slower hopeful ending.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson for the facts that protect you.
